note: THE STRONGEST CASE IN THIS SET, and the only one whose baseline is not a reconstruction. EngineHub bumped snakeyaml 1.26 -> 1.33 AND applied the fix in the SAME commit, so state 1 runs the version they were actually on. Compare infoarchive (bump and fix two years apart, so the pairing of code and version is assembled) and membrane (no baseline constructible at all, because its jackson requires snakeyaml 2.x).

NOT found by the bump-axis mine, which checked 94 rows of this break and produced four candidates, all false on reading.

bump_source: snakeyaml 1.32 release; DoS hardening (CVE-2022-38749..38752 family). The fix commit is dated 2022-09-26, days after 1.32 shipped.

behavioral_break.mechanism: snakeyaml 1.32+ caps incoming documents at 3 MiB (3145728 code points) BY DEFAULT. WorldEdit built its parser as `new Yaml(new SafeConstructor(), representer, options)` — no LoaderOptions — so the new default applied the moment they crossed the boundary, and any config file above 3 MiB stopped loading.
behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: Same as `mechanism`; recorded under both names because older cases in this directory use `why_it_breaks` and newer ones use `mechanism`, and nothing normalises them yet.
behavioral_break.observed_exception: org.yaml.snakeyaml.error.YAMLException: The incoming YAML document exceeds the limit: 3145728 code points.
behavioral_break.blast_radius: Clients loading YAML above 3 MiB. For WorldEdit that is real: Minecraft server configs and region data commonly exceed it, which is presumably why they chose a 64 MB ceiling rather than a modest bump.

adaptation.repo_note: WorldEdit, the Minecraft world-editing engine. Multi-module Gradle (Kotlin DSL); worldedit-core holds the YAML config processor.
adaptation.commit_message: Use SnakeYaml 1.32+, set loader code point limit. (#2194)
adaptation.the_call: LoaderOptions loaderOptions = new LoaderOptions(); int yamlCodePointLimit = Integer.getInteger("worldedit.yaml.codePointLimit", 64 * 1024 * 1024); loaderOptions.setCodePointLimit(yamlCodePointLimit); yaml = new Yaml(new SafeConstructor(), representer, dumperOptions, loaderOptions);
adaptation.why_that_matters: The default is 64 MB, so the limit is genuinely lifted. Contrast swagger-parser@93d1f495, bspfsystems@b0eb7bbc, jenkinsci/pipeline-utility-steps-plugin@78e3face and jenkinsci/configuration-as-code-plugin@652ee9ba: all four added the same knob but left the default at 3 MB. Those are configurability changes, not recoveries, and cannot produce a differential for ANY input size. Five for five, the split follows what the project IS: libraries and plugins pass the decision to their users; applications lift the limit.
adaptation.author_awareness: They wrapped the call in `catch (NoSuchMethodError ignored) { // pre-1.32 snakeyaml }`, so the authors knew the behaviour was version-dependent and that the method did not exist before the boundary.

verification.method: 3-state differential over the real production entry point. Compiled worldedit-core's YAMLProcessor with javac and -sourcepath, letting the compiler resolve 17 classes from their own source tree (YAMLNode, YAMLFormat, Vector3, ...), plus guava 31.1-jre and jsr305 3.0.2. Gradle was not used: the verifier drives Maven, and a full Gradle build is unnecessary to isolate this path.
verification.test: Driver.java (authored). Writes a valid WorldEdit-style config of N MB to a temp file, then calls new YAMLProcessor(file, false).load() and reads a property back. Authored because their tests have no 4 MB config — the reason membrane's own test states outright: fixtures that large are generated, never committed.
